1.title: Soil Types of the Foothills
1.html:
Granite / gneiss terroir → colluvial-alluvial soils, acidic to leached brown soils (arènes granitiques — fertile sandy weathering layers)
Schist terroir → brown, stony, clayey soils
Volcano-sedimentary terroir → varied brown soils rich in fertile elements
Sandstone terroir → leached brown soils to podzols; sandy, light, thin and poor

💡 Podzol is a distinctive poor soil: a humus layer on top, below it a pale grey silica-rich layer, and below that a deposit layer alternating black (humus) and rust-coloured (iron) bands.
2.title: Soil Types of the Sub-Vosges Hills
2.html:
Limestone terroir → browned black calcareous residual soils (rendzina)
Calcareous sandstone terroir → brown, stony, dry soils
Clayey marl terroir → heavy, poorly drained but fertile
Marl-limestone terroir → reddish-brown rendzina, extremely favourable to viticulture

Within these soils a relatively rare type, "calcareous sandstone" (calcaro-gréseux), has moderate to low mineral content — this relative poverty lets Sylvaner show an elegant, tight backbone and lets Gewurztraminer develop a fine structure, often with attractive tropical fruit notes.
3.title: Soils of the Rhine Plain: Loess and Lehm
3.html:
Loess: wind-deposited fine sediment (particles under 62 microns) made of sand, clay and limestone; extremely fertile.
Lehm: decalcified, brown loess (in the upper part of the loess layer), forming brown calcareous soils and pararendzina.
Alluvial terroir: clayey sandy soils, gravelly and less developed; in places pseudogley — acidic brown soils formed by long-standing waterlogging.
4.question: Relatively poor calcareous sandstone (calcaro-gréseux) soils bring out the best style in which two varieties?
4.options.1: Sylvaner (elegant, tight backbone) and Gewurztraminer (fine structure)
4.explanation: Calcareous sandstone soils have moderate to low mineral content and are relatively poor. This lets Sylvaner develop an elegant, tight backbone and Gewurztraminer show a fine structure, and the resulting wines often carry attractive tropical fruit notes.
5.keyPoints.0: Foothills: granite / gneiss, schist, volcano-sedimentary, sandstone (poor podzols)
5.keyPoints.1: Sub-Vosges hills: limestone, calcareous sandstone (good for Sylvaner / Gewurztraminer), clayey marl, marl-limestone
5.keyPoints.2: Rhine plain: loess (very fertile), Lehm, alluvial soils (occasional pseudogley)
